app.title: RAG World
app.subtitle: Maturity map and registry of RAG technologies

link.guardedWhy: The address answers but refuses to show itself to a robot, as publishers and some platforms do. The portal checks its links itself and cannot confirm this one, so it does not present it as checked. Opening it by hand works as usual.

map.title: RAG maturity map
map.subtitle: Position shows evidence-backed maturity and the attention a technology receives. Data is rebuilt automatically.
map.howToRead:
How to read this map

• Horizontal position is the maturity level from L0 (hypothesis) to L6 (industry standard). The level is computed by a rule from collected evidence, never assigned by hand.
• Vertical position is attention: citation velocity normalised within the work's age cohort. Where a cohort holds fewer than five works there is nothing to normalise against: the measured velocity is shown, and it is not comparable with normalised values. Attention is not evidence that something works.
• Colour marks the stratum of decisions, shape marks the kind of object.
• Opacity reflects confidence in the level: fewer fresh verified pieces of evidence, paler point.
• This is not an adoption recommendation: the map reports confirmed maturity, it does not advise what to pick.
• Click a point to open the technology card with its evidence and the reasoning behind its level.
map.unavailable: Map unavailable: data artifact not found
map.attentionOrigin: Citation velocity divided by the median of works of the same year. Above one means the technology is discussed more actively than its peers.
map.attentionNotNormalized: The age cohort holds fewer than five works, so its median is unstable and no normalisation is applied. The measured citations per month are shown; they are not comparable with normalised values.

registry.title: RAG technology registry
registry.subtitle: The single source of facts about RAG technologies. Every view on this portal reads from here.
registry.howToRead:
What this is

Each record carries verifiable facts: source links, kind of object, its configuration in the dimension schema, and the residual — mechanisms the schema does not express. The maturity level is computed from evidence and always comes with that evidence listed.
registry.unavailable: Registry unavailable: data artifact not found

techCard.notFound: Technology not found in the registry
techCard.residual: Residual: not expressed by the schema
techCard.whyLevelPending: The full derivation will appear together with the maturity journal.
techCard.nextLevel: What is missing for the next level
techCard.noEvidence: No evidence collected yet, so no level was computed. This means missing data, not an immature technology.
techCard.skippedText: Conditions for {{levels}} are not met. This is not an error: the scale allows an industry path — documented production use confirms that something works without a publication. Otherwise a widely used technique would rank below a preprint nobody reproduced.
techCard.configurationReviewed: Values checked against the primary source on {{date}}. A match with the base configuration here is the result of that check, not the absence of one.
techCard.configurationUnreviewed: The configuration has not been derived from sources: the values shown are the base ones and assert nothing about this technology.
techCard.variableNote: "Chosen at run time" means the system varies this value by query or by mode; the value recorded is the one from the fullest branch.
techCard.inapplicableNote: "Does not apply" means the object has no such stage: a value here would assert something about a thing that does not exist.
techCard.basisRussianOnly: This justification is in Russian. It states what the primary source says and what follows from it, and its translation is deliberately not machine-made: a mistranslated claim would change what the portal says about the technology.

about.title: About
about.intro: RAG World collects verifiable information about Retrieval-Augmented Generation technologies. The portal reports what has been proposed, what corroborates it, and how a technology's standing changes over time. Every claim comes with the evidence needed to check it yourself.
about.howLevelsText: The maturity level is computed by a rule from collected evidence: publications, repository state, presence in frameworks, documented production use. The same evidence always yields the same level, so any value reproduces on a repeat run. Where no machine-readable source exists, a person enters the evidence with a link to its confirmation, and such a record is marked separately.
about.howUpdatesText: Collection runs from open sources on a weekly schedule. While serving, the portal reads pre-built files and never contacts those sources, so their failure ages the data while the portal keeps working. The build date and a staleness marker are always shown on the front page.
about.limitsText: Open indexes do not know everything. Some publications exist only on platforms without digital identifiers, and production use has no machine-readable source at all. A record without a level means the data on it is insufficient. Levels are comparable within one kind of object: a technique enters a framework as a single function, while a full architecture travels the same path with markedly more difficulty.
about.dataText: The data is open and machine-readable. It can be downloaded whole, cited, and used to check any claim the portal makes.

about.fileMap: maturity map points with level history

levelCondition.L3: L3 — needs buildable open source from the authors
levelCondition.L4: L4 — needs an independent implementation, framework presence, or package downloads
levelCondition.L6: L6 — needs independent implementations from at least three vendors

digest.title: Digest
digest.subtitle: A periodic summary of registry changes. Each issue covers the period since the previous one and lists the records that received a level for the first time, rose and fell, along with the number of evidence items collected and sources checked.
digest.provenance: The text of an issue is assembled by a template from registry data, without a language model. An issue never changes after publication. Under each one you can expand the records its changes are drawn from.
digest.firstIssue: first issue: covers everything accumulated so far
digest.showBasis: show what the issue rests on ({{count}})
digest.first: received level {{level}} for the first time
digest.noTranslation: This issue was published before the English localisation and exists in Russian only.

notFound.title: No such page
notFound.body: This address does not match any section of the portal. It may contain a typo, or the record was renamed.
notFound.brokenBody: Something went wrong while building it. The rest of the portal works — try starting from the map or the registry.

residuals.title: Residual queue
residuals.subtitle: A mechanism whose working the dimension schema cannot describe is recorded against a technology as a residual. Here the residuals of every record are brought together and counted.
residuals.rule: A mechanism met in {{threshold}} or more records becomes a candidate for a new dimension of the schema. One met once or twice remains a particularity of individual works.
residuals.candidatesFound: Candidate dimensions: {{count}}. Extending the schema is decided separately, since a new dimension changes the formal model and its description.

article.foundationsNote: This text explains what the rest rests on: why there are twenty-eight dimensions, why index topology is separated from the search operator, and what a residual means. The registry and the map report facts about technologies, and those facts are checked by collectors. Here is the model that gives the facts meaning, and no collector can confirm it — it is justified by reasoning. As standalone work the text is published separately; on the portal it serves as the foundation.
